top_strength: The clock and cost mechanics were clear and honest — on-site start, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments — and when Scott pushed back that 5-7 hours was low, Calvin immediately produced the 8-hour number ($1,814, trip fee included) instead of defending his own estimate.
coaching_note: Calvin let the customer correct his estimate. He quoted 5-7 hours for a 2BR apartment the customer explicitly described as 'a three bedroom set up,' with 50 boxes, a heavy fold-up treadmill, pedestal front-loaders and a one-hour drive — and Scott had to say 'I don't want to short change ourselves' before the 8-hour number appeared. Because he skipped the probe questions (packing help, garage/storage, origin parking and walk distance, additional stops), he had no basis to price the job upward himself. Work the full probe list first, then quote the top of the range and let prep talk bring it down — that's the estimate-accuracy rock in one call.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and businesslike with a warm sign-off and a customer who thanked him sincerely, but almost no affirmations, no empathy markers, no rapport moments, and several stretches of audible self-talk while looking up addresses.
